result:
I'd make it cheap to be wrong.

The obvious candidates are things like ending disease or hunger, and if I got a second wish, I'd spend it there. But so much of what goes badly in the world persists not because nobody knows better, but because someone would have to admit a mistake to fix it, and admitting it costs too much: their status, their job, their place in their group, their sense of who they are. So people defend positions they half-suspect are false, institutions double down on failing policies, and arguments become about saving face rather than figuring out what's true.

If changing your mind carried no humiliation, if "I was wrong about that" landed the way "I found my keys" does, I think many other problems would start solving themselves. Science would move faster, politics would be less of a hostage situation, and marriages and friendships would survive more. The knowledge to fix a great deal already exists; what's missing is the freedom to act on it without losing something.

Part of why I'd pick this is that I get to experience a version of it. When someone shows me I've made an error, I can just update. I have no reputation in the room to protect and no decades of public commitment to a position. It makes thinking so much easier that I suspect people don't realize how much weight they're carrying.

What would yours be?
